outcome: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: 253 pregnant women with COVID-19 who delivered at a tertiary care center in north Kerala, India, between April 15, 2020, and October 31, 2020
finding: Increased maternal age, obesity, nulliparity, fetal growth restriction, preterm rupture of membranes, meconium staining of amniotic fluid, cardiotocogram abnormalities and active COVID-19 infection at the time of birth were associated with increased cesarean section rates in COVID-19 positive pregnancies.
gest_age: N/A - Term and preterm deliveries were included in the analysis, but the specific ranges were not defined within the abstract
